page.layout: One printed page, one text column at right with a narrow margin column at left. Running head at top. Full-width epigraph verse block above the heading; then the chapter heading and the main text column top to bottom; left margin holds notes "De Elementis." and "Elementum." Text continues below the column with a catchword-like word "dicun" at the foot.

main_text.p: Sex Nonas Majus, October, Julius & Mars, Quatuor at reliqui, dabit Idus quilibet octo, Inde dies reliquos omnes dic esse Calendas.
main_text.head: CAPUT TERTIUM. De ΣΤΟΙΧΕΙΟΛΟΓΙΑ VULGARI, ET PRIMO de Elemento Ignis.
main_text.p: De Elementis.Dhuc fuit Corpus inanimatum aethereum in Coelo & Stellis: Inanimatum corpus Sublunare sequitur, quod sub aethereo corpore Mundi à Deo conditore collocatum subsistit: adeoq; aetheris ambitu continetur.
Est hoc aut Primarium, aut Secundarium.
Primarium Sublunare inanimatum corpus est principium quoddam secundarii, & sequentium animatorum corporum. Diciturq; Elementum.Elementum.
ELEMENTA sunt corpora inanimata sublunaria primaria, dicta Simplicia, ex quibus corpora secundaria sublunaria & animata reliqua, quæ mixta dicun

page.notes: The left margin notes "De Elementis." and "Elementum." are placed at the start of their paragraphs. The first word of the chapter body is a large decorated initial "A" joined to "Dhuc" as printed ("ADhuc" rendered as "Dhuc" beside the initial; the initial letter is likely A). The Greek heading ΣΤΟΙΧΕΙΟΛΟΓΙΑ is transcribed as printed. The final word "dicun" is printed at the foot and is the catchword-style continuation; the line continues on the next page. Show-through text in the background is not transcribed.
